City overview
Economic Development

This category covers projects aimed at developing the city's economy. Their goal is to improve the quality of urban infrastructure and services and to raise residents' quality of life.

1 - Neighbourhood Economy Model
Why should you cross the whole city for everything when it can be done locally? The project supports the creation of local small markets, community gardens, repair workshops, family services and community enterprises. Residential communities can shape their surroundings based on their own ideas and needs, while new jobs and more accessible services are created. The development strengthens neighbourhood ties and can save residents time and money.
Finance
Startup cost: 6,000
Running cost: 2,400
Investment: 18,000
Development support from the partner company: 3,000

Unemployment: -0.3%
Number of small companies: 0.04%
Start
2 - Commercial and Cultural Centre
A vibrant city centre with an international atmosphere is created, where commerce, culture and community life meet. The development expands the existing commercial district with modern shops, restaurants, services, residential buildings and community spaces. Public spaces are renewed, pedestrian and transport connections improve, and the area becomes tidier and more liveable. The investment creates new jobs, supports local businesses and makes the area more liveable and attractive.
Finance
Startup cost: 28,000
Running cost: 8,000
Investment: 120,000
Development support from the partner company: 25,000


Effects

Population conditions/satisfaction: 0.8%

Unemployment: -0.8%
Number of small companies: 0.06%
Number of medium companies: 1%
Start
3 - Local Food Supply
By modernising the four existing farmers' markets and expanding their range, fresh local food becomes available in more places. New sales points, refrigeration and storage facilities are built, and an online marketplace enables pre-ordering and local pick-up. Regular gastronomic and family programmes make the markets more attractive. The development increases local producers' revenues, creates new sales opportunities and jobs, reduces food transport needs and makes shopping more convenient for residents.
Finance
Startup cost: 7,000
Running cost: 1,500
Investment: 25,000
Development support from the partner company: 3,000

Business-friendliness: 0.6%
Sustainability: 0.4%

Waste management situation: 0.3%
Digitalization: 0.3%
Healthcare: 0.1%
Social: 0.2%

Unemployment: -0.2%
Number of small companies: 0.03%

4 - Circular Economy Pilot Project
What is waste for one company can be a valuable raw material for another! Within the project, the municipality and local companies set up a joint system for recycling industrial by-products, waste and surplus energy. New collection, processing and material-exchange solutions are launched, reducing landfilling, energy consumption and pollution. The development lowers businesses' operating costs and creates new business opportunities and green jobs.
Finance
Startup cost: 8,000
Running cost: 2,000
Investment: 33,000
Development support from the partner company: 14,000


Effects
Business-friendliness: 0.4%
Sustainability: 1.5%
Air quality: 0.3%
Waste management situation: 3%
Digitalization: 0.1%
Settlement development: 0.3%
Population conditions/satisfaction: 0.2%
Population education level: 0.2%
Unemployment: -0.2%
Number of small companies: 0.02%
Number of medium companies: 1%

5 - Corporate Social Responsibility Platform
Local large companies and the municipality create a joint platform that links companies' support opportunities with the district's development and community needs. Companies contribute financial support, expertise, equipment and volunteer work to educational, social, environmental and community programmes. Coordinated cooperation provides more resources for local initiatives and improves public services and residents' quality of life, while strengthening companies' local ties.
Finance
Startup cost: 3,000
Running cost: 2,000
Investment: 2,000
Development support from the partner company: 15,000


Effects
Sustainability: 0.1%
Administration: 0.5%
Housing management: 0.1%
Digitalization: 0.1%
Educational institutions: 0.3%
Culture: 0.2%
Population conditions/satisfaction: 0.4%
Population education level: 0.3%
Start
6 - Economic and Employment Cooperation
Local businesses, the municipality, employment organisations and training institutions launch a joint programme to expand employment. Job placement tailored to companies' labour needs, vocational training, retraining and subsidised employment programmes help people find work. Special attention is paid to career starters and disadvantaged jobseekers. The cooperation reduces local unemployment and labour shortages, supports small businesses and increases residents' incomes.
Finance
Startup cost: 5,000
Running cost: 8,000
Investment: 3,000
Development support from the partner company: 2,000


Effects
Business-friendliness: 0.7%
Educational institutions: 0.3%
Social: 0.4%

Population conditions/satisfaction: 0.3%
Working conditions: 0.2%
Population education level: 0.5%
Unemployment: -1%
Number of small companies: 0.01%
Number of medium companies: 1%
Start
7 - Local Economic Development Innovation and Knowledge Centre
Local economic development is brought together by a new knowledge and innovation centre built on cooperation between the municipality, businesses and professional partners. The centre continuously analyses economic processes, monitors the results of development projects, identifies new investment opportunities and supports innovative initiatives. Regular research, professional programmes and knowledge sharing lead to better-founded municipal decisions, more efficient use of resources and more successful economic development.
Finance
Startup cost: 6,000
Running cost: 12,000
Investment: 15,000
Development support from the partner company: 8,000

Administration: 0.7%
Digitalization: 0.5%
Settlement development: 0.1%
Population education level: 0.2%
Number of small companies: 0.01%
Start
8 - Smart Economy Applications
A new digital platform connects local businesses, the municipality and residents. Companies can access economic information, funding opportunities, advice and business partners in one place, while residents can more easily find local services. Data-driven and geospatial solutions support investment planning, city operations and economic decisions. The development reduces administrative burdens, improves the efficiency of public services and strengthens the competitiveness of local businesses.
Finance
Startup cost: 4,000
Running cost: 3,000
Investment: 22,000
Development support from the partner company: 3,500


Effects
Business-friendliness: 0.5%
Administration: 1.1%
Digitalization: 2%
Working conditions: 0.3%
Number of small companies: 0.03%

9 - Community Funding System
Residents and local businesses can jointly fund the developments that matter to them. On a new online platform, anyone can explore projects awaiting support, make a financial contribution and follow how the collected funds are used. The contributions can fund playgrounds, community spaces, green areas and local civic initiatives. The system brings new resources into urban development, speeds up smaller investments and strengthens residents' participation in local affairs.
Finance
Startup cost: 2,500
Running cost: 1,500
Investment: 6,500
Development support from the partner company: 12,000


Effects
Sustainability: 0.2%
Administration: 0.3%
Housing management: 0.1%
Digitalization: 0.5%

Culture: 0.2%

10 - Innovation Fund
The municipality and local companies set up a jointly financed innovation fund that supports new technological, economic and social solutions through calls for proposals. The funds finance smart city developments, environmental projects, digital services and innovations of local businesses. Grants are awarded based on expected results and feasibility. The fund stimulates new investments, attracts further development resources and strengthens the competitiveness of the local economy.
Finance
Startup cost: 3,500
Running cost: 14,000
Investment: 12,000
Development support from the partner company: 10,000


Effects
Business-friendliness: 1%
Sustainability: 0.2%
Administration: 0.1%

Working conditions: 0.4%

Number of small companies: 0.04%

11 - Local Crisis Fund
Local small businesses receive quick financial help when unexpected economic difficulties threaten their operations. The municipality, companies and other supporters set up a joint crisis fund that helps struggling companies with preferential bridging loans, non-repayable grants and business advice. The programme primarily supports smaller shops, service providers and start-ups. Its aim is to preserve jobs, prevent business closures and strengthen the stability of the local economy.
Finance
Startup cost: 3,000
Running cost: 5,000
Investment: 18,000
Development support from the partner company: 8,000


Effects
Business-friendliness: 0.4%
Administration: 0.1%
Digitalization: 0.2%
Social: 0.3%
Population conditions/satisfaction: 0.1%
Working conditions: 0.2%
Unemployment: -0.6%
Number of small companies: 0.02%

12 - Housing and Premises Management
By modernising municipal rental flats and commercial premises, and by involving privately owned properties, new housing and community opportunities are created. The programme renovates run-down flats, puts vacant premises to use and offers affordable rental options for people in need, young people and local businesses. The development increases the utilisation of property assets, improves housing conditions, revitalises community life in the neighbourhoods and increases the municipality's rental income.
Finance
Startup cost: 8,000
Running cost: -12,000
Investment: 75,000
Development support from the partner company: 5,000


Effects
Business-friendliness: 0.3%
Sustainability: 0.4%
Waste management situation: 0.1%
Administration: 0.2%
Housing management: 3%
Digitalization: 0.1%
Public safety: 1%
Social: 1%
Ratio of people in a poor social situation: -1.6%
Settlement development: 0.2%
Population conditions/satisfaction: 0.6%
Unemployment: -0.2%
Number of small companies: 0.03%
Start
13 - IT Development
Replacing the municipality's own IT systems with a unified system, with the necessary infrastructure investments and partial digitalisation of internal processes (enterprise information system).
Finance
Startup cost: 12,000
Running cost: -8,800
Investment: 43,000
Development support from the partner company: 0


Effects
Administration: 4%
Digitalization: 3%
Population conditions/satisfaction: 0.7%
Working conditions: 1.3%
Population education level: 0.6%
Start
14 - New Customer Service Centre
A new, barrier-free municipal customer service centre is established at 26 Állomás Street, bringing the most important administrative services for residents and businesses together in one place. Digital administration, online appointment booking and modern reception areas reduce waiting times and the number of in-person visits. The renovation of the building tidies up the surroundings, and energy-efficient operation lowers maintenance costs. The development results in faster administration, more efficient municipal operations and higher resident satisfaction.
Finance
Startup cost: 0
Running cost: 0
Investment: 0
Development support from the partner company: 0
